summary: Petition under Section 79(1) (b) read with Section 79(1) (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 inter-alia seeking compensation on account of occurrence of ‘Change in Law events’ and/or Force Majeure events relating to Power Purchase Agreement dated 19.8.2013 entered into between the Petitioner and the Respondents. 2. The Petitioner had filed the present Petition seeking adjustment of tariff on account of Change in Law and Force Majeure events after 27.2.2013 (cut-off date) affecting the Project during the Operating Period in order to restore the Petitioner to the same economic position as the events had not occurred in terms of the TANGEDCO PPA. The Petitioner made the following prayers: _“a) Declare that the events enumerated in Paras 6 and 7 of the Petition constitute Change in Law events as per the provisions of the PPA and that the Petitioner is entitled to be restored to the same economic condition prior to occurrence of the said Changes in Law events;_ _c) Direct the Respondent to continue to make payments accrued in favor of the Petitioner on account of Change in Law events enumerated in Paras 6 and 7 of the Petition from 01.08.2016 uptill the effect of the said Change in Law events or validity of the PPA;_ _d) Without prejudice and strictly in alternative to prayer (a) to (c), declare that the events enumerated in Paras 6 and 7 of the Petition constitute Force Majeure events as per the provisions of the PPA and that the Petitioner is entitled to be restored to the same economic condition prior to occurrence of the said Force Majeure events;_ _f) Direct the Respondent to continue to make payments accrued in favor of the Petitioner on account of Force Majeure events enumerated in Paras 6 and 7 of the Petition from 01.08.2016 uptill the effect of the said Force Majeure events or validity of the PPA;_ _under the PPA on account of the events enumerated in Paras 6 and 7 of the Petition;_ _i) In the interim, pending final adjudication of the present Petition, direct the Respondent to make payment of Rs. 81.28 crores i.e. 90% of the already incurred amount by the Petitioner from 01.08.2015 to 31.07.2016 towards supply of power to the Respondent in order to ease the cash crunch faced by the Petitioner;_ _j) Pass such other and further order or orders as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice”._ 3. The Commission, _vide_ its order dated 19.12.2017, examined the Force Majeure and Change in Law claims of the Petitioner, and the gist of the findings of the Commission in order dated 19.12.2017, are tabulated herein below: 6. As regards Appeal No. 225/2018 is concerned, the Petitioner challenged the Commission’s order dated 19.12.2017 on the following grounds: _While Counsel on both sides are in agreement that the Appellant is entitled to compensation for the actual Station Heat Rate, and that this issue is covered by orders of the Supreme Court, learned Counsel for the Respondents would submit that the dispute is not regarding the Appellant’s entitlement, but their failure to place relevant material before the CERC which was the reason for the CERC being forced to adopt the rate, stipulated in the Schedule to the PPA, as the Station Heat Rate; and, having failed to provide the necessary information before the CERC, the Appellant cannot now claim the benefit of the judgment of the Supreme Court._ _observations made in the Order passed by it earlier, i.e in the order which has now been set aside. All other claims stand dismissed, and the Appeal stands disposed of accordingly.”_ 8. Pursuant to the APTEL’s remand, the matter was listed for the hearing on 18.10.2023. The learned counsel for DBPL, during the course of the hearing, submitted that the Commission in another similarly placed matter i.e. Petition No. 101/MP/2017 has permitted the Petitioner DBPL (also the Petitioner in the present case) to place on record the computation of claims in terms of the APTEL judgment in Appeal No. 253 of 2018. Therefore, the same directions are required to be issued in the present matter in light of the judgment of the APTEL in Appeal No. 225 of 2018 dated 25.7.2023. The Respondent TANGEDCO was also directed to file its submissions in the matter. The Petitioner filed its compliance affidavit on 15.1.2024 10. The matter was further listed for the hearing on 24.1.2024 along with Petition No. 101/MP/2017, comprising similar issues as in the present matter. The Commission permitted the Petitioner to file rejoinders in both matters. Further, TANGEDCO was also permitted to file its reply to the compliance affidavit dated 15.1.2024, filed by the Petitioner. TANGEDCO filed its reply dated 1.4.2024, in response to the compliance affidavit filed by the Petitioner. 14. The matter was further listed on 17.10.2024, and the order was reserved after considering the detailed submissions made by the learned counsels of the parties. 17. The Respondent, TANGEDCO, has submitted that the claims of the Petitioner ought to be considered by the Commission strictly in terms of the applicable regulations, subject to a strict prudence check. 21. Furthermore, it is observed that the Petitioner has also submitted a copy of the _ The extent of loss they have suffered, as a result of belated payment of compensation for change in law to them by the 2nd Respondent, is a question of fact which necessitates consideration on the basis of the documentary evidence adduced _ 27. With this order, the directions of the APTEL in Appeal No. 225 of 2018 stand implemented, and the Petition stands disposed of to the extent of the remand.
